relevance_note: The cohort includes four patients with A20 haploinsufficiency carrying heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants ("A20 haploinsufficiency (four patients)"; Table 3 Pt. 40-43).
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; values were typed from my reading into a Python script in my scratch directory, which only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Scope: this is a multi-disease Indian SAID cohort (Pt. 1-49); only the four TNFAIP3/A20 haploinsufficiency patients (Table 3, Pt. 40-43) and the two relatives of Pt. 40 described with clinical or genetic information (her mother and younger brother) are extracted; patients with other SAID genes are out of scope for this HA20 extraction and were not entered. Table 3 is a patients-as-rows table; the Markdown wraps each 'Molecular details' cell onto a new line after the gene symbol, so variant spans quote that continuation line (the line directly after the patient's row). Relatives: 'Mother' and 'Younger brother' are Pt. 40's mother and younger brother (no family labels in the paper). The mother's variant is given only as 'same variant'; I recorded Pt. 40's c.1504C>T/p.Arg502Trp for her with both spans. The younger brother has recurrent oral ulcers but 'does not carry this variant', so he has no variants row. Inheritance for Pt. 40 recorded as 'inherited maternal' because the mother is stated to be heterozygous for the same variant; the father is not mentioned. Pathogenicity for Pt. 40 is only described in the text as 'a novel variant'. Pt. 41/42/43 variant classes are not described in words (only HGVS), so variant_type is 'not reported'. Age column of Table 3 is 'age of diagnosis'; recorded as age_at_diagnosis. Country 'India' comes from the cohort-level statement. Publication-level 'cites_prior_report' is true for the cohort (refs 14, 17, 19, 26, 27), but none of the four TNFAIP3 rows carries a reference marker; those references concern non-HA20 patients (MVK, NLRP12, SAVI, DIRA, LACC1 per the reference list). Checklist choices: Pt. 40 ANA/ANCA negative and 'Gut Biopsy: no vasculitis' are narrower than the checklist items 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' and 'vasculitis', so those stay 'not reported' (the specific absences are in phenotypic_features). Pt. 40 'central nervous system involvement' marked observed from persistent headache, papilledema and type 2 Arnold Chiari malformation on brain MRI. Pt. 42 'autoantibodies' marked observed from 'AIHA' with 'Direct coombs test 3+'. Pt. 43 'Osteomyelitis/CGD' is a single osteomyelitis entry; 'recurrent infections' left not reported. Immunoglobulin and lymphocyte values for Pt. 41/42 have no reference ranges or interpretation, so they were not turned into features. 'refectory ulcers requiring repeated hospitalization' (Pt. 40) is ambiguous as to site and was not recorded as a separate feature. The cohort inclusion statement (all included patients fulfilled the ESID definition, which requires recurrent fever and raised inflammatory markers) was not used to infer phenotypes, because the paper contradicts it elsewhere (e.g. Pt. 24 with negative NLRP3 screening and Pt. 25/26 with mutation screening 'under process' are tabulated). Contradictions/inconsistencies noted: Results say VUS patients inconsistent with the clinical profile were excluded, yet Pt. 42 and Pt. 43 (TNFAIP3 VUS; AIHA/immune deficiency and osteomyelitis/CGD) are listed under A20 haploinsufficiency; Pt. 40's onset is '6 M' in Table 3 while the text says she 'was 2 years old when she had presented' (presentation, not necessarily onset).
